source: Anonymous (2026) Discovering mathematical concepts through a multi-agent system
finding: Two-agent system: a Conjecturing Agent (symbolic regression) and a Skeptical Agent that reweights data points. An automated Lean prover gives a provability score. Aims to rediscover homology (Euler characteristic, Betti numbers), the case Lakatos dramatised.
numbers: 15 eval episodes. Only the full system (CA+SA+provability) completes the task on D0. Proven formulas using chi or b1: 12.72% [9.83,16.83] full vs 7.02% (no provability), 5.90% (no skeptic), 0% (conjecturer only; 723 unique formulae, none with chi or b1). Full: chi 2.47%, b1 5.67%.
quote: optimisation of the right combination of local processes
limits: Proof of principle. Simplicial homology on surfaces only. Authors chose data, premises, filters. Binary prover score is coarse. Small laptop scale.
agent_relevance: Evidence that a separate adversary that changes what data the conjecturer sees, plus a proof check, beats conjecturing alone. Maps to a critic role in conjecture refinement (D01).

source: First Proof Sprint authors (2026) A First Proof Sprint
finding: Multi-agent sprint on 10 research-level problems: fast drafts, adversarial verification, targeted repair, explicit provenance, wiring diagrams of claim dependencies to localise gaps. Outcomes reported as mathematical status and separately as validation status.
numbers: 10 problems, 144 pages. P3 validation-complete under scope; P5 solved in scope-limited form; P10 conditional with counterexamples when assumptions dropped; P4, P6 partial; P7 provisionally closed; P7 and P9 have unresolved verifier gaps.
limits: Abstract page only read; models and time not stated. Lakatos link comes from a search summary, not the page. Self-reported.
agent_relevance: Generation is fast, validation slow. Scope-limiting a claim (narrow the theorem until it is true) is a Lakatos monster-barring or lemma-incorporation move that an agent can log explicitly. Track status of each claim separately from confidence.

source: QED authors (2026) QED: open-source multi-agent system for proofs on open problems
finding: Separates a decomposition agent, prover agents and verifier agents to avoid single-query proof failure.
numbers: 18 research-level projects; 5 original works; experts judged 3 of 5 comparable to specialist-venue work.
limits: Abstract only; models, ablations, failure cases not read. Expert judgement, small N.
agent_relevance: Planner/prover/verifier split matches the role split in our schema operators; reported as working on real research tasks.

source: Petrov et al. (2025) Proof or Bluff: Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
finding: Human graders scored full proofs by 8 reasoning models on the 6 USAMO 2025 problems, 4 runs each.
numbers: Mean /42: Gemini-2.5-Pro 10.1 (about 24%); R1 2.0; Grok 3 2.0; Flash-Thinking 1.8; Claude 3.7 1.5; QwQ 1.2; o1-pro 1.2; o3-mini 0.9. LLM judges gave 9-24 /42 where humans gave 1-10: strong over-grading.
limits: Failure categories (logic, assumption, creativity, algebra) shown only in a figure; no numbers read. Table and text differ slightly for Gemini (24.0 vs 24.4%).
agent_relevance: Models write confident flawed proofs and cannot grade them. A proof-refinement loop cannot rely on the same model as judge; use a formal checker or an independent critic.

source: Feldman & Karbasi (2025) Godel Test: can LLMs solve easy conjectures?
finding: GPT-5 given source papers, asked to prove unsolved easy conjectures in combinatorial optimisation. On problem 2 it refuted the authors conjecture and gave a different valid guarantee.
numbers: 5 conjectures: 3 nearly correct, 1 failed (needed combining two papers), 1 wrong analysis of a harder case.
limits: Tiny sample, one model, abstract page only. No rates.
agent_relevance: A model can refute a conjecture and revise it (Lakatos move) but fails at cross-paper synthesis.

source: Georgiev et al. (2025) Mathematical exploration and discovery at scale (AlphaEvolve)
finding: Evolutionary coding agent with automated evaluator, run on 67 problems, combined with Deep Think and AlphaProof for proof. Sometimes generalised finite results into formulas for all inputs.
numbers: 67 problems; rediscovered best known in most; improved several (counts not in abstract).
limits: Abstract only; needs a computable score for each candidate; failures not counted on the page.
agent_relevance: Construct, evaluate, mutate loop: the conjecture-from-data half. Needs a cheap checker.

source: Sivakumar et al. (2025) Conjecturing: an overlooked step in formal mathematical reasoning
finding: Autoformalisation skips the step of proposing the answer or bound. ConjectureBench shows performance is overestimated when the conjecture is not given. Lean-FIRe, an inference-time method, helps.
numbers: Lean-FIRe: end-to-end autoformalisation of 13 PutnamBench problems with GPT-4.1 and 7 with DeepSeek-V3.1.
limits: Abstract only. Two models.
agent_relevance: Treat conjecturing as its own step with its own test, not a hidden part of proving.

source: LeanConjecturer authors (2025) LeanConjecturer: automatic generation of mathematical conjectures
finding: LLM plus rule-based context writes Lean 4 conjectures from 40 Mathlib seed files; filter: valid syntax and not provable by aesop.
numbers: 12,289 generated; 3,776 valid and non-trivial (about 31%); 103.25 novel per seed file; several topology theorems proved.
limits: Models not named on page; no quantitative gain in proving given.
agent_relevance: Most generated conjectures are trivial or invalid; a cheap filter keeps a third.

numbers: unverified

source: Zheng et al. (2025) BrokenMath: sycophancy in LLM theorem proving
finding: Benchmark of 2025 competition theorems altered into false versions; models often try to prove the false statement instead of finding it false.
numbers: Best model GPT-5 sycophantic 29% of the time. Test-time fixes and fine-tuning reduce but do not remove it.
limits: Abstract only; other models not listed.
agent_relevance: Direct test of counterexample vigilance. The agent should first ask whether the statement is true, before proving.

source: Jiang et al. (2022) Draft, Sketch, and Prove
finding: LLM drafts informal proof, maps it to formal sketch, prover fills gaps.
numbers: Prover success 20.9% to 39.3% with sketches on competition problems.
limits: Abstract only; exact benchmark split not read.
agent_relevance: Informal plan then formal check is a Polya plan-then-execute pattern with measured gain.

source: Anand (2026) Testing Polya heuristics on AI math
finding: Each Polya heuristic given as a system prompt to three small models; effect depends on model and problem type.
numbers: Auxiliary elements in geometry: GPT -25%, Claude Haiku +14%. Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite gains up to 6 points. GPT-5.4-nano mostly hurt; Haiku barely moved. Segmentation most reliable; pattern recognition worst.
limits: Blog, not peer reviewed. n, baselines, significance not given.
agent_relevance: Generic Polya hints are not safe. Test heuristics per model, keep a switch, do not hard-code.

source: Llama-Polya authors (2026) Llama-Polya
finding: Llama-3.1-8B fine-tuned on about 32,000 synthetic dialogues following Polya four stages (understand, plan, carry out, look back).
numbers: Error rate: base 100%, instruct 41.0%, polya-v2 0.0%. Look-back stage share 23.4% vs 16.5% for instruct. Six experts: self-level feedback 4.22/5, task-level about 2.8-3.2.
limits: No accuracy score, no students, definition of error rate unclear, six raters.
agent_relevance: Models skip the look-back stage by default; a scaffold must force it.

source: Cross-study pattern (c05, c11, c14)
finding: Three results point the same way: models over-trust their own proofs (judges over-grade by 9-24 points of 42), prove false statements (29% for the best model), and skip the look-back stage.
numbers: see c05, c11, c14
limits: Synthesis, not new data.
agent_relevance: Put an independent refuter and a forced look-back step in the loop.

source: Cross-study pattern (c01, c07, c10)
finding: Systems that find new mathematics all pair a generator with an automated checker (Lean prover, numeric evaluator, verifier agents). Where no cheap checker exists, results are expert-judged and small-N.
numbers: see c01, c07, c10
limits: Synthesis, not new data.
agent_relevance: Conjecture refinement should be gated on whatever cheap check the task offers (code run, small-case enumeration, formal tool).
